$comment: Hand-maintained. Declares the LAYERED governance packages that control this repository, how their integrity is verified, and — since AWE-0 — how each accepted architecture package is bound to the repository's ADR, module-state and Horizon authority. Verified in CI by scripts/check-network-governance.mjs (integrity) and scripts/check-architecture-governance.mjs (binding). This file exists separately from handoff-provenance.json on purpose: that file is regenerated wholesale by scripts/sync-handoff.mjs, which rebuilds its object from HANDOFF_VERSION/HANDOFF_SOURCE and preserves only `overrides`, so any layer declaration added there would be silently dropped on the next `pnpm sync:handoff`. Overloading its single handoffVersion string to mean three packages would also make the base-layer provenance check ambiguous.
subordination: Network architecture is ADDITIVE and SUBORDINATE to the production handoff and to the security, privacy, tenant-isolation, authority, resilience and non-regression requirements that precede it. Where a network requirement and a security requirement conflict, the stricter restriction wins and the network requirement yields. No layer below may be weakened to simplify a layer above.

architectureGovernance.$comment: AWE-0. Closes W01-F-GOV-01 and the root defect recorded in docs/agentic-architecture-review/01_PACKAGE_INVENTORY_AND_PRECEDENCE.md §3.1-§3.2: six accepted architecture packages (567 tracked files) were substantive and internally coherent while being declared nowhere, verified by nothing, and connected to no accepted ADR in either direction. Registration binds a package to authority. It NEVER confers any. Revised after an independent adversarial review; see docs/governance/AWE_0_ARCHITECTURE_GOVERNANCE_WIRING.md for what each rule here does and does not prove.

mandate.$comment: AWE-0 is not self-authorised. Owner ruling 2, recorded in the merged security/resilience record, both froze installed packages and directed that later handoff pointers live in a registry OUTSIDE them. This file is that registry. The clause below is verified verbatim by scripts/check-architecture-governance.mjs, so the citation cannot drift from the text it cites. It is a merged governance record, not an ADR, and is not citable as a per-package adrRelation.
mandate.clause:
Future additive handoff pointers belong in a **top-level handoff registry or index maintained
   outside older checksummed packages** — not inside them.
mandate.immutabilityClause:
An installed versioned handoff package becomes **immutable after installation**, except through an
   explicitly approved corrective amendment.

authorizationLadder: ARCHITECTURE EXISTS — files are on disk under docs/production-handoff/.
ARCHITECTURE IS ACCEPTED — the package is declared here with governanceStatus=accepted and its manifest verifies. This is the highest rung any declaration in this file can reach.
IMPLEMENTATION IS AUTHORIZED — config/scope/module_states.yaml puts the module in an implementable state at or below horizon_authorized. Read, never declared here.
CAPABILITY IS IMPLEMENTED — code, migrations and tests exist and pass.
CAPABILITY IS CERTIFIED/LIVE — the applicable acceptance gate is signed and the module is activated.
architectureGovernance.implementationAuthorityRule: Every governed package declares implementationAuthority="none" and no other value is accepted. It is a restatement of rung 2, not a choice: a package cannot self-declare authorized, implemented, certified or live, because the fields that decide those live in config/scope/module_states.yaml and in signed gates. The validator READS module state per package and reports what it observes; the registry never asserts it.
architectureGovernance.runtimeAuthorityRule: No runtime gate may read this file. scripts/check-architecture-governance.mjs scans every JS/TS source file under packages/ — every extension the repository can execute, every directory, not just src/ — and fails if any references the registry. What that proves and what it does not is stated in the gate's own "WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM" note: it detects a literal reference, not a dynamically constructed one. The material control is the ladder itself — the registry grants nothing, so reading it would gain a caller nothing.
architectureGovernance.evidenceRule: An `evidence` string is HUMAN-REVIEWED RATIONALE. No validator proves it true. What the validator proves is: the authority exists, is source-qualified, is Accepted, the relation kind is in the vocabulary, and the whole binding still matches the digest a reviewer signed off in scripts/lib/governance-layers.mjs. Semantic correctness of the rationale is an architecture-review obligation and is labelled as one rather than implied to be machine-checked.

authorityModel.$comment: Replaces the dense 1..N precedence ordering the first AWE-0 candidate carried. An independent review found that ordering over-strong and inert: it implied a total 'later package wins' rank across packages that are frequently INCOMPARABLE — v1.6.0 brokerage and FacilityOS say nothing about each other — and nothing in the repository consumed it. Authority is a small lattice over CLASSES plus strictest-wins, not a rank over instances.

classes.base: The preserved v1.2 handoff: constitution, sequencing doctrine, activation gates.
classes.controlling: Security, privacy, tenant isolation, authority, resilience. Never yields.
classes.additive-subordinate: Additive design. Yields to base and controlling. Mutually INCOMPARABLE.

resolution: A controlling requirement beats any additive-subordinate requirement.
A base requirement beats any additive-subordinate requirement.

Two additive-subordinate packages are INCOMPARABLE. Being installed later confers nothing. Where two of them overlap on a module and genuinely disagree, that is a conflict to record in unresolvedAuthority, not a tie to break by version order.
Regardless of class, the stricter accepted restriction wins. Security, tenant-isolation, authority, privacy, legal, resilience and certification constraints fail closed.
Class is anchored to the layer's root path in scripts/lib/governance-layers.mjs and cannot be changed by editing this file. A layer cannot demote its own authority out of the rules that bind it.
authorityModel.answerable: Which packages apply to module X (a SET, computed by the validator from moduleScope and printed), which class outranks which (the lattice above), which module-state gate applies (config/scope/module_states.yaml), which Horizon applies (horizon_authorized), and which authority governs a subject (adrRelations).

authorityAboveArchitecture: adr/ — accepted repository ADRs, cited as ADR-NNNN, enforced in code
docs/decisions/ — accepted network decision records, cited as ADR-NNNNN (N-qualified)
config/scope/module_states.yaml — machine-readable module and Horizon authority, enforced by scripts/validate-scope.mjs

authoritySources.$comment: adr/ and docs/decisions/ reuse all eighteen numbers 0001-0018, so a bare four-digit reference is ambiguous between an Accepted repository ADR and a frequently Proposed network decision. The repository already disambiguates them — docs/decisions/ records title themselves `ADR-N0018` and declare `**ADR ID:** N0018`, and that form is used in runtime source, migrations, a CI gate, nine governance documents and six tests — so AWE-0 adopts the existing convention rather than inventing one. Counts are declared so a new collision is a reviewed two-line diff.

expectedRelationCounts.$comment: Tallied by kind so that silently downgrading a governed-by to a weaker relation — the move that erases a real binding while leaving the gate green — is a two-line diff. Update both in the same change, deliberately.

ciWiring.$comment: The gates that must actually RUN. The predecessor of this block asserted only that ci.yml CONTAINED these filenames, which a YAML comment, an echo, `run: true # node ...`, `if: false` or `continue-on-error: true` all satisfy while the gate never executes or never blocks. The rule is now about the parsed workflow.

adrRelationVocabulary.governed-by: The record rules the matter. Where the package and the record differ, the record wins.
adrRelationVocabulary.constrained-by: The record bounds the package without deciding its content.
adrRelationVocabulary.additive-beneath: The package adds detail under the record and does not touch its decision.

architectureGovernance.unresolvedAuthorityRule: An architecture claim with no accepted authority behind it belongs in `unresolvedAuthority`, which may not name an authority. Each item carries a stable id, and the inventory of known ids is anchored in scripts/lib/governance-layers.mjs: declaring more is always allowed, but an id may only DISAPPEAR by being moved into RESOLVED_AUTHORITY with the accepted authority that closed it. Registering a package resolves nothing it leaves open.

architectureExemption.note: handoff-provenance.json names this root as handoffSource and pins all 45 generated copies to it, and CI runs `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt` against it directly. Its authority is anchored outside this registry — it is the only layer for which that is true.

layers.note: The base handoff. Its integrity is verified in CI by `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`, and its generated operational copies at the repository root are verified by scripts/check-handoff-provenance.mjs. handoff-provenance.json describes THIS layer only.

architectureExemption.note: The controlling security layer. Its role is anchored to this root in scripts/lib/governance-layers.mjs and cannot be claimed or renounced by editing this file. It is the layer the subordination clause above says never yields, so it is not architecture bound BY the model — it is part of what binds.

layers.note: Controlling security layer. Generates no root copies. Its manifest was unverified by CI before N0 — the same gap the audit found in v1.4.0, and it is closed by the same validator.

architectureExemption.note: Unlike the six architecture packages, v1.4.0 is already joined to the decision record: ADR-N0014 (docs/decisions/0014-n4-transactional-transport-intent.md, Accepted) cites this root by path, and the N0-N7 workstream produced sixteen decision records against it. The validator verifies that citation rather than accepting this claim; measured across all nine layers, no other root scores above zero.

layers.note: Network architecture. Additive and subordinate. Installing it authorizes no runtime behavior: no participants, integrations, agents, dispatch, marketplace or settlement activate because a document describes them.

Enterprise agent operations. Self-declared: "additive to all existing FreightOS production handoffs, especially v1.3.0 Security/Privacy/Resilience and v1.4.0 Network Architecture. It does not replace or weaken any existing accepted requirement." moduleScope is the reviewed registration act this file exists to hold; the package itself names no module id from config/scope/module_states.yaml.

adrRelations.evidence: ADR-0013 authorizes Horizon 1 production implementation only and preserves the rest of the ecosystem as contracts, schemas, disabled configuration, fixtures and simulation. It is the decision that lets this package be complete design while remaining unimplementable, and where the package differed it would win.

ADR-0014 fixes the handoff tree as docs/production-handoff/ rather than docs/handoff/, which is why this package sits where it does. Its immutability and provenance clauses are scoped to the v1.2 preserved package — handoff-provenance.json covers that root only — so they do not reach this package. What byte-pins this package is its own MANIFEST.json, verified by scripts/check-network-governance.mjs.

ADR-0004 decides that agents never write directly to domain tables and that mutations use validated handlers, policy, approvals, transactions and audit. An enterprise agent-operations design may not introduce an action path that bypasses that boundary.

ADR-0018 computes effective autonomy as the minimum of the declared ceiling, the module ceiling and the horizon ceiling, and forbids any code path that raises it. scripts/validate-scope.mjs clamps every agent to that. No agent-operations design raises it.

ADR-0012 decides to add FacilityOS as the origin/destination operational coordination layer and a provider-independent Autonomous Vehicle Gateway over the mode-neutral core, and rules that provider-specific APIs must not define the FreightOS domain. Where this package and that decision differ, ADR-0012 wins.

ADR-0011 separates freight mission orchestration from safety-critical motion control: no dynamic driving task, robotics, PLC, conveyor, dock restraint, safety interlock or industrial motion command. scripts/validate-scope.mjs enforces the verb list in CI.

ADR-0025 does not merely bound detention, it decides it: a required policy-field table, the clock-start and stop derivation, the state machine, fail-closed POLICY_REQUIRED when no active policy exists, and a prohibition on any code-level default free-time allowance. FacilityOS 11_APPOINTMENTS_CAPACITY_AND_DETENTION.md leaves those open, so the repository is ahead of the package and ADR-0025 governs.
